hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: If people are together in one contract of mukatabah (contract for gradual emancipation), their master should not free anyone of them without consulting his companions who are with him in the mukatabah and obtaining their consent. If they are young, their consultation means nothing and that is not valid for them. He said: This is because a man might strive for all the people and fulfill their mukatabah so that their emancipation is completed through him. Then the master goes to the one who is fulfilling on their behalf and through whom is their salvation from slavery and frees him. That would be incapacity for those who remain of them. He only intended by that advantage and increase for himself. That is not valid for those who remain of them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'There is no harm and no reciprocating harm.' And this is the most severe harm. Malik said regarding slaves who are given mukatabah together: Their master may free from among them the old one who is senile and the young one who cannot fulfill anything, neither of them having any help or strength in their mukatabah, so that is permitted for him.

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 إِذَا كَانَ الْقَوْمُ جَمِيعًا فِي كِتَابَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ، لَمْ يُعْتِقْ سَيِّدُهُمْ أَحَدًا مِنْهُمْ ، دُونَ مُؤَامَرَةِ أَصْحَابِهِ الَّذِينَ مَعَهُ فِي الْكِتَابَةِ وَرِضًا مِنْهُمْ ، وَإِنْ كَانُوا صِغَارًا فَلَيْسَ مُؤَامَرَتُهُمْ بِشَيْءٍ وَلَا يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ . قَالَ : وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ رُبَّمَا كَانَ يَسْعَى عَلَى جَمِيعِ الْقَوْمِ وَيُؤَدِّي عَنْهُمْ كِتَابَتَهُمْ لِتَتِمَّ بِهِ عَتَاقَتُهُمْ ، فَيَعْمِدُ السَّيِّدُ إِلَى الَّذِي يُؤَدِّي عَنْهُمْ وَبِهِ نَجَاتُهُمْ مِنَ الرِّقِّ فَيُعْتِقُهُ ، فَيَكُونُ ذَلِكَ عَجْزًا لِمَنْ بَقِيَ مِنْهُمْ ، وَإِنَّمَا أَرَادَ بِذَلِكَ الْفَضْلَ وَالزِّيَادَةَ لِنَفْسِهِ ، فَلَا يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى مَنْ بَقِيَ مِنْهُمْ ، وَقَدْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : " لَا ضَرَرَ وَلَا ضِرَارَ " . وَهَذَا أَشَدُّ الضَّرَرِ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي الْعَبِيدِ يُكَاتَبُونَ جَمِيعًا : /10 إِنَّ لِسَيِّدِهِمْ أَنْ يُعْتِقَ مِنْهُمُ الْكَبِيرَ الْفَانِيَ ، وَالصَّغِيرَ الَّذِي لَا يُؤَدِّي وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمَا شَيْئًا ، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا عَوْنٌ وَلَا قُوَّةٌ فِي كِتَابَتِهِمْ ، فَذَلِكَ جَائِزٌ لَهُ /10 .

hadiths.english_translation: Malik said regarding a man who gives mukatabah to his slave, then the mukatab dies and leaves his umm walad, and there remains upon him some of his mukatabah payment, but he leaves enough to fulfill what is upon him: His umm walad is a slave owned when the mukatab did not become free until he died and did not leave a child who would be freed by paying what remains, so his umm walad would be freed by their freedom. Malik said regarding a mukatab who frees a slave of his or gives some of his wealth in charity, and his master did not know about that until the mukatab became free. Malik said: That is executed upon him and the mukatab cannot retract it. If the master of the mukatab knew before the mukatab became free and rejected that and did not permit it, then if the mukatab becomes free while that is in his possession, he is not required to free that slave nor to give that charity, except if he does so willingly of his own accord.

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي الرَّجُلِ يُكَاتِبُ عَبْدَهُ ، ثُمَّ يَمُوتُ الْمُكَاتَبُ وَيَتْرُكُ أُمَّ وَلَدِهِ ، وَقَدْ بَقِيَتْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ كِتَابَتِهِ بَقِيَّةٌ ، وَيَتْرُكُ وَفَاءً بِمَا عَلَيْهِ : /10 إِنَّ أُمَّ وَلَدِهِ أَمَةٌ مَمْلُوكَةٌ حِينَ لَمْ يُعْتَقْ الْمُكَاتَبُ حَتَّى مَاتَ وَلَمْ يَتْرُكْ وَلَدًا ، فَيُعْتَقُونَ بِأَدَاءِ مَا بَقِيَ ، فَتُعْتَقُ أُمُّ وَلَدِ أَبِيهِمْ بِعِتْقِهِمْ . /10 قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي الْمُكَاتَبِ يُعْتِقُ عَبْدًا لَهُ أَوْ يَتَصَدَّقُ بِبَعْضِ مَالِهِ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِذَلِكَ سَيِّدُهُ حَتَّى عَتَقَ الْمُكَاتَبُ ، قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 يَنْفُذُ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ ، وَلَيْسَ لِلْمُكَاتَبِ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ فِيهِ ، فَإِنْ عَلِمَ سَيِّدُ الْمُكَاتَبِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَعْتِقَ الْمُكَاتَبُ ، فَرَدَّ ذَلِكَ وَلَمْ يُجِزْهُ ، فَإِنَّهُ إِنْ عَتَقَ الْمُكَاتَبُ وَذَلِكَ فِي يَدِهِ ، لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعْتِقَ ذَلِكَ الْعَبْدَ وَلَا أَنْ يُخْرِجَ تِلْكَ الصَّدَقَةَ ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَفْعَلَ ذَلِكَ طَائِعًا مِنْ عِنْدِ نَفْسِهِ /10 .$E419

hadiths.english_translation: Chapter: The bequest concerning the mukatab

Malik said: The best of what I have heard regarding a mukatab whom his master frees at death is that the mukatab is valued according to his condition - if he were sold, that would be the price he would reach. If the value is less than what remains upon him of the mukatabah, that is placed in the third of the deceased, and one does not look to the number of dirhams that remained upon him. That is because if he were killed, his killer would not pay except his value on the day he killed him, and if he were injured, the one who injured him would not pay except the blood money of his injury on the day he injured him. One does not look in any of that to what he was contracted for of dinars and dirhams, because he is a slave as long as anything remains upon him of his mukatabah. If what remained upon him of his mukatabah is less than his value, only what remained upon him of his mukatabah is counted in the third of the deceased, and that is because the deceased only left for him what remained upon him of his mukatabah, so it became a bequest he bequeathed to him. Malik said: The explanation of that is that if the value of the mukatab was one thousand dirhams, and only one hundred dirhams remained of his mukatabah, and his master bequeathed to him the one hundred dirhams that remained upon him, it is counted for him in the third of his master, and he became free by it. Malik said regarding a man who gave mukatabah to his slave at his death: He is valued as a slave, and if there is capacity in his third for the price of the slave, that is permitted for him. Malik said: The explanation of that is that the value of the slave is one thousand dinars, so his master gives him mukatabah for two hundred dinars at his death, and the third of his master's wealth is one thousand dinars, so that is permitted for him, and it is only a bequest he bequeathed to him in his third. If the master had bequeathed to people with bequests, and there is no surplus in the third over the value of the mukatab, the mukatab is given priority, because mukatabah is emancipation and emancipation is given priority over bequests. Then those bequests are placed in the mukatabah of the mukatab - they follow him with it, and the heirs of the testator are given choice. If they wish to give the people of bequests their complete bequests and the mukatabah of the mukatab is theirs, that is for them. If they refuse and hand over the mukatab and what is upon him to the people of bequests, that is for them, because the third went to the mukatab, and because every bequest anyone bequeathed. If the heirs say: What our companion bequeathed is more than his third and he took what is not his, he said: His heirs are given choice, and it is said to them: Your companion bequeathed what you know. If you wish to execute that for its people according to what the deceased bequeathed, otherwise hand over to the people of bequests the third of all the deceased's wealth. He said: If the heirs hand over the mukatab to the people of bequests, the people of bequests have what is upon him of mukatabah. If the mukatab fulfills what is upon him of mukatabah, they take that in their bequests according to their shares. If the mukatab is incapacitated, he becomes a slave for the people of bequests and does not return to the people of inheritance, because they left him when they were given choice, and because the people of bequests when he was handed over to them guaranteed him. If he died, they would have nothing against the heirs. If the mukatab dies before he fulfills his mukatabah and leaves wealth that is more than what is upon him, his wealth is for the people of bequests. If the mukatab fulfills what is upon him, he is freed and his loyalty returns to the family of the one who contracted his mukatabah. Malik said regarding a mukatab upon whom his master has ten thousand dirhams, then he waives from him at his death one thousand dirhams. Malik said: The mukatab is valued and it is looked at - how much is his value? If his value is one thousand dirhams, then what was waived from him is one-tenth of the mukatabah, and that in value is one hundred dirhams, which is one-tenth of the value. So one-tenth of the mukatabah is waived from him, and that becomes one-tenth of the value in cash. That is only like if all that was upon him were waived, and if he did that, only the value of the mukatab would be counted in the third of the deceased's wealth - one thousand dirhams. If what was waived from him is half the mukatabah, half the value is counted in the third of the deceased's wealth. If it is less than that or more, it is upon this calculation. Malik said: When a man waives from his mukatab at his death one thousand dirhams from ten thousand dirhams, and he does not specify that it is from the beginning of his mukatabah or from its end, one-tenth is waived from him from every installment. Malik said: When a man waives from his mukatab at death one thousand dirhams from the beginning of his mukatabah or from its end, and the original mukatabah was for three thousand dirhams, the mukatab is valued at cash value, then that value is divided and that thousand that is from the beginning of the mukatabah is given its share from that value, according to its proximity to the term and its merit, then the thousand that follows the first thousand according to its merit also, then the thousand that follows it according to its merit also, until its end is reached. Each thousand has merit according to its position in hastening the term and delaying it, because what is delayed of that is less in value. Then the amount that befalls that thousand from the value is placed in the third of the deceased according to the variation of that, whether little or much, it is upon this calculation. Malik said regarding a man who bequeathed to a man a quarter of a mukatab or freed a quarter of him, then the man perished and then the mukatab perished and left much wealth - more than what remained upon him. Malik said: The heirs of the master and the one to whom a quarter of the mukatab was bequeathed are given what remained for them upon the mukatab, then they divide what is surplus. The one to whom a quarter of the mukatab was bequeathed has a third of what is surplus after fulfilling the mukatabah, and the heirs of his master have two-thirds. That is because the mukatab is a slave as long as anything remains upon him of his mukatabah, so he is only inherited by slavery. Malik said regarding a mukatab whom his master freed at death, he said: If the third of the deceased does not carry him, he is freed from him the amount that the third carried, and the amount of that is waived from him from the mukatabah - if upon the mukatab is five thousand dirhams and his value is two thousand dirhams in cash, and the third of the deceased is one thousand dirhams, half of him is freed and half the mukatabah is waived from him. Malik said regarding a man who said in his will: My slave so-and-so is free, and give mukatabah to so-and-so: Emancipation is given priority over mukatabah.

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 إِنَّ أَحْسَنَ مَا سَمِعْتُ فِي الْمُكَاتَبِ يُعْتِقُهُ سَيِّدُهُ عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ ، أَنَّ الْمُكَاتَبَ يُقَامُ عَلَى هَيْئَتِهِ تِلْكَ الَّتِي لَوْ بِيعَ كَانَ ذَلِكَ الثَّمَنَ الَّذِي يَبْلُغُ ، فَإِنْ كَانَتِ الْقِيمَةُ أَقَلَّ مِمَّا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْكِتَابَةِ ، وُضِعَ ذَلِكَ فِي ثُلُثِ الْمَيِّتِ ، وَلَمْ يُنْظَرْ إِلَى عَدَدِ الدَّرَاهِمِ الَّتِي بَقِيَتْ عَلَيْهِ ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ لَوْ قُتِلَ لَمْ يَغْرَمْ قَاتِلُهُ إِلَّا قِيمَتَهُ يَوْمَ قَتْلِهِ ، وَلَوْ جُرِحَ لَمْ يَغْرَمْ جَارِحُهُ إِلَّا دِيَةَ جَرْحِهِ يَوْمَ جَرَحَهُ . وَلَا يُنْظَرُ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ إِلَى مَا كُوتِبَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الدَّنَانِيرِ وَالدَّرَاهِمِ ، لِأَنَّهُ عَبْدٌ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ كِتَابَتِهِ شَيْءٌ ، وَإِنْ كَانَ الَّذِي بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ كِتَابَتِهِ أَقَلَّ مِنْ قِيمَتِهِ ، لَمْ يُحْسَبْ فِي ثُلُثِ الْمَيِّتِ إِلَّا مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ كِتَابَتِهِ ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا تَرَكَ الْمَيِّتُ لَهُ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ كِتَابَتِهِ ، فَصَارَتْ وَصِيَّةً أَوْصَى بِهَا /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَتَفْسِيرُ ذَلِكَ : أَنَّهُ لَوْ كَانَتْ قِيمَةُ الْمُكَاتَبِ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ ، وَلَمْ يَبْقَ مِنْ كِتَابَتِهِ إِلَّا مِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ ، فَأَوْصَى سَيِّدُهُ لَهُ بِالْمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ الَّتِي بَقِيَتْ عَلَيْهِ ، حُسِبَتْ لَهُ فِي ثُلُثِ سَيِّدِهِ فَصَارَ حُرًّا بِهَا /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي رَجُلٍ كَاتَبَ عَبْدَهُ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ : /10 إِنَّهُ يُقَوَّمُ عَبْدًا ، فَإِنْ كَانَ فِي ثُلُثِهِ سَعَةٌ لِثَمَنِ الْعَبْدِ جَازَ لَهُ ذَلِكَ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَتَفْسِيرُ ذَلِكَ : أَنْ تَكُونَ قِيمَةُ الْعَبْدِ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ ، فَيُكَاتِبُهُ سَيِّدُهُ   عَلَى مِائَتَيْ دِينَارٍ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ ، فَيَكُونُ ثُلُثُ مَالِ سَيِّدِهِ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ ، فَذَلِكَ جَائِزٌ لَهُ ، وَإِنَّمَا هِيَ وَصِيَّةٌ أَوْصَى لَهُ بِهَا فِي ثُلُثِهِ ، فَإِنْ كَانَ السَّيِّدُ قَدْ أَوْصَى لِقَوْمٍ بِوَصَايَا ، وَلَيْسَ فِي الثُّلُثِ فَضْلٌ عَنْ قِيمَةِ الْمُكَاتَبِ بُدِئَ بِالْمُكَاتَبِ ، لِأَنَّ الْكِتَابَةَ عَتَاقَةٌ وَالْعَتَاقَةُ تُبَدَّأُ عَلَى الْوَصَايَا ، ثُمَّ تُجْعَلُ تِلْكَ الْوَصَايَا فِي كِتَابَةِ الْمُكَاتَبِ يَتْبَعُونَهُ بِهَا وَيُخَيَّرُ وَرَثَةُ الْمُوصِي ، فَإِنْ أَحَبُّوا أَنْ يُعْطُوا أَهْلَ الْوَصَايَا وَصَايَاهُمْ كَامِلَةً ، وَتَكُونُ كِتَابَةُ الْمُكَاتَبِ لَهُمْ ، فَذَلِكَ لَهُمْ ، وَإِنْ أَبَوْا وَأَسْلَمُوا الْمُكَاتَبَ وَمَا عَلَيْهِ إِلَى أَهْلِ الْوَصَايَا ، فَذَلِكَ لَهُمْ ، لِأَنَّ الثُّلُثَ صَارَ فِي الْمُكَاتَبِ ، وَلِأَنَّ كُلَّ وَصِيَّةٍ أَوْصَى بِهَا أَحَدٌ .E420 فَقَالَ الْوَرَثَةُ : الَّذِي أَوْصَى بِهِ صَاحِبُنَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْ ثُلُثِهِ ، وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مَا لَيْسَ لَهُ ، قَالَ : فَإِنَّ وَرَثَتَهُ يُخَيَّرُونَ ، فَيُقَالُ لَهُمْ : قَدْ أَوْصَى صَاحِبُكُمْ بِمَا قَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ ، فَإِنْ أَحْبَبْتُمْ أَنْ تُنَفِّذُوا ذَلِكَ لِأَهْلِهِ عَلَى مَا أَوْصَى بِهِ الْمَيِّتُ ، وَإِلَّا فَأَسْلِمُوا لِأَهْلِ الْوَصَايَا ثُلُثَ مَالِ الْمَيِّتِ كُلِّهِ . قَالَ : فَإِنْ أَسْلَمَ الْوَرَثَةُ الْمُكَاتَبَ إِلَى أَهْلِ الْوَصَايَا ، كَانَ لِأَهْلِ الْوَصَايَا مَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْكِتَابَةِ ، فَإِنْ أَدَّى الْمُكَاتَبُ مَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْكِتَابَةِ ، أَخَذُوا ذَلِكَ فِي وَصَايَاهُمْ عَلَى قَدْرِ حِصَصِهِمْ ، وَإِنْ عَجَزَ الْمُكَاتَبُ كَانَ عَبْدًا لِأَهْلِ الْوَصَايَا ، لَا يَرْجِعُ إِلَى أَهْلِ الْمِيرَاثِ ، لِأَنَّهُمْ تَرَكُوهُ حِينَ خُيِّرُوا ، وَلِأَنَّ أَهْلَ الْوَصَايَا حِينَ أُسْلِمَ إِلَيْهِمْ ضَمِنُوهُ   ، فَلَوْ مَاتَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ عَلَى الْوَرَثَةِ شَيْءٌ ، وَإِنْ مَاتَ الْمُكَاتَبُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُؤَدِّيَ كِتَابَتَهُ وَتَرَكَ مَالًا هُوَ أَكْثَرُ مِمَّا عَلَيْهِ ، فَمَالُهُ لِأَهْلِ الْوَصَايَا ، وَإِنْ أَدَّى الْمُكَاتَبُ مَا عَلَيْهِ عَتَقَ وَرَجَعَ وَلَاؤُهُ إِلَى عَصَبَةِ الَّذِي عَقَدَ كِتَابَتَهُ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي الْمُكَاتَبِ يَكُونُ لِسَيِّدِهِ عَلَيْهِ عَشَرَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ ، فَيَضَعُ عَنْهُ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ ، قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 يُقَوَّمُ الْمُكَاتَبُ فَيُنْظَرُ كَمْ قِيمَتُهُ ؟ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ قِيمَتُهُ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ ، فَالَّذِي وُضِعَ عَنْهُ عُشْرُ الْكِتَابَةِ ، وَذَلِكَ فِي الْقِيمَةِ مِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ وَهُوَ عُشْرُ الْقِيمَةِ ، فَيُوضَعُ عَنْهُ عُشْرُ الْكِتَابَةِ ، فَيَصِيرُ ذَلِكَ إِلَى عُشْرِ الْقِيمَةِ نَقْدًا ، وَإِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ كَهَيْئَتِهِ لَوْ وُضِعَ عَنْهُ جَمِيعُ مَا عَلَيْهِ ، وَلَوْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ لَمْ يُحْسَبْ فِي ثُلُثِ مَالِ الْمَيِّتِ إِلَّا قِيمَةُ الْمُكَاتَبِ أَلْفُ دِرْهَمٍ ، وَإِنْ كَانَ الَّذِي وُضِعَ عَنْهُ نِصْفُ الْكِتَابَةِ ، حُسِبَ فِي ثُلُثِ مَالِ الْمَيِّتِ نِصْفُ الْقِيمَةِ ، وَإِنْ كَانَ أَقَلَّ مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ فَهُوَ عَلَى هَذَا الْحِسَابِ /10 .E421 قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 إِذَا وَضَعَ الرَّجُلُ عَنْ مُكَاتَبِهِ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ مِنْ عَشَرَةِ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ ، وَلَمْ يُسَمِّ أَنَّهَا مِنْ أَوَّلِ كِتَابَتِهِ أَوْ مِنْ آخِرِهَا ، وُضِعَ عَنْهُ مِنْ كُلِّ نَجْمٍ عُشْرُهُ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَإِذَا وَضَعَ الرَّجُلُ عَنْ مُكَاتَبِهِ عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ مِنْ أَوَّلِ كِتَابَتِهِ أَوْ مِنْ آخِرِهَا ، وَكَانَ أَصْلُ الْكِتَابَةِ عَلَى ثَلَاثَةِ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ قُوِّمَ الْمُكَاتَبُ قِيمَةَ النَّقْدِ ، ثُمَّ قُسِمَتْ   تِلْكَ الْقِيمَةُ فَجُعِلَ لِتِلْكَ الْأَلْفِ الَّتِي مِنْ أَوَّلِ الْكِتَابَةِ حِصَّتُهَا مِنْ تِلْكَ الْقِيمَةِ ، بِقَدْرِ قُرْبِهَا مِنَ الْأَجَلِ وَفَضْلِهَا ، ثُمَّ الْأَلْفُ الَّتِي تَلِي الْأَلْفَ الْأُولَى بِقَدْرِ فَضْلِهَا أَيْضًا ، ثُمَّ الْأَلْفُ الَّتِي تَلِيهَا بِقَدْرِ فَضْلِهَا أَيْضًا ، حَتَّى يُؤْتَى عَلَى آخِرِهَا ، تَفْضُلُ كُلُّ أَلْفٍ بِقَدْرِ مَوْضِعِهَا فِي تَعْجِيلِ الْأَجَلِ وَتَأْخِيرِهِ ، لِأَنَّ مَا اسْتَأْخَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ كَانَ أَقَلَّ فِي الْقِيمَةِ ، ثُمَّ يُوضَعُ فِي ثُلُثِ الْمَيِّتِ ، قَدْرُ مَا أَصَابَ تِلْكَ الْأَلْفَ مِنَ الْقِيمَةِ عَلَى تَفَاضُلِ ذَلِكَ ، إِنْ قَلَّ أَوْ كَثُرَ فَهُوَ عَلَى هَذَا الْحِسَابِ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي رَجُلٍ أَوْصَى لِرَجُلٍ بِرُبُعِ مُكَاتَبٍ ، أَوْ أَعْتَقَ رُبُعَهُ ، فَهَلَكَ الرَّجُلُ ثُمَّ هَلَكَ الْمُكَاتَبُ ، وَتَرَكَ مَالًا كَثِيرًا أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ ، قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 يُعْطَى وَرَثَةُ السَّيِّدِ وَالَّذِي أَوْصَى لَهُ بِرُبُعِ الْمُكَاتَبِ مَا بَقِيَ لَهُمْ عَلَى الْمُكَاتَبِ ، ثُمَّ يَقْتَسِمُونَ مَا فَضَلَ فَيَكُونُ لِلْمُوصَى لَهُ بِرُبُعِ الْمُكَاتَبِ ، ثُلُثُ مَا فَضَلَ بَعْدَ أَدَاءِ الْكِتَابَةِ وَلِوَرَثَةِ سَيِّدِهِ الثُّلُثَانِ . وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ الْمُكَاتَبَ عَبْدٌ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ كِتَابَتِهِ شَيْءٌ ، فَإِنَّمَا يُورَثُ بِالرِّقِّ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي مُكَاتَبٍ أَعْتَقَهُ سَيِّدُهُ عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ ، قَالَ : /10 إِنْ لَمْ يَحْمِلْهُ ثُلُثُ الْمَيِّتِ عَتَقَ مِنْهُ قَدْرُ مَا حَمَلَ الثُّلُثُ ، وَيُوضَعُ عَنْهُ مِنَ الْكِتَابَةِ قَدْرُ ذَلِكَ ، إِنْ كَانَ عَلَى الْمُكَاتَبِ خَمْسَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ وَكَانَتْ قِيمَتُهُ أَلْفَيْ دِرْهَمٍ نَقْدًا ، وَيَكُونُ ثُلُثُ الْمَيِّتِ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ عَتَقَ نِصْفُهُ وَيُوضَعُ عَنْهُ شَطْرُ   الْكِتَابَةِ /10 .E422 قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي رَجُلٍ قَالَ فِي وَصِيَّتِهِ : غُلَامِي فُلَانٌ حُرٌّ ، وَكَاتِبُوا فُلَانًا : /10 تُبَدَّأُ الْعَتَاقَةُ عَلَى الْكِتَابَةِ /10 .E423 /1 كِتَاب الْمُدَبَّرِ /1

hadiths.english_translation: Chapter: The Mudabbar (slave promised freedom after master's death)

Malik narrated to me that he said: The practice among us regarding one who grants tadbir to his slave woman, then she gives birth to children after his granting her tadbir, then the slave woman dies before the one who granted her tadbir: Her children are in the same position as her - the same condition that was established for her is established for them, and their mother's death does not harm them. When the one who granted her tadbir dies, they are freed if the third accommodates them. Malik said: Every female with kinship ties - her child is in the same position as her. If she is free and gives birth after her emancipation, her child is free. If she is mudabbara or mukataba or freed to certain years or given for service or part of her is free or pledged or umm walad, the child of each one of them is according to the example of their mother's condition - they are freed by her freedom and enslaved by her slavery. Malik said regarding a mudabbara who was granted tadbir while she was pregnant, and her master did not know of her pregnancy: Her child is in the same position as her, and that is only like a man who freed his slave woman while she was pregnant and did not know of her pregnancy. Malik said: The sunnah regarding her is that her child follows her and is freed by her freedom. Malik said: Likewise, if a man purchased a slave woman while she was pregnant, the slave woman and what is in her belly belong to the one who purchased her, whether the purchaser stipulated that or not. Malik said: It is not lawful for the seller to exclude what is in her belly, because that is uncertainty that decreases from her price, and he does not know whether that will reach him or not. That is only like if he sold a fetus in its mother's belly, and that is not lawful for him because it is uncertainty. Malik said regarding a mukatab or mudabbar - one of them purchased a slave woman, had intercourse with her, she became pregnant from him and gave birth: The child of each one of them from his slave woman is in the same position as him - they are freed by his freedom and enslaved by his slavery. Malik said: When he is freed, his umm walad is property from his property that is handed over to him when he is freed.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي /12 مَالِك /12 ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : /10 الْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا فِيمَنْ دَبَّرَ جَارِيَةً لَهُ ، فَوَلَدَتْ أَوْلَادًا بَعْدَ تَدْبِيرِهِ إِيَّاهَا ، ثُمَّ مَاتَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ قَبْلَ الَّذِي دَبَّرَهَا : إِنَّ وَلَدَهَا بِمَنْزِلَتِهَا ، قَدْ ثَبَتَ لَهُمْ مِنَ الشَّرْطِ مِثْلُ الَّذِي ثَبَتَ لَهَا ، وَلَا يَضُرُّهُمْ هَلَاكُ أُمِّهِمْ ، فَإِذَا مَاتَ الَّذِي كَانَ دَبَّرَهَا ، فَقَدْ عَتَقُوا إِنْ وَسِعَهُمُ الثُّلُثُ /10 . وَقَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 كُلُّ ذَاتِ رَحِمٍ فَوَلَدُهَا بِمَنْزِلَتِهَا ، إِنْ كَانَتْ حُرَّةً ، فَوَلَدَتْ بَعْدَ عِتْقِهَا فَوَلَدُهَا أَحْرَارٌ ، وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مُدَبَّرَةً أَوْ مُكَاتَبَةً أَوْ مُعْتَقَةً إِلَى سِنِينَ أَوْ مُخْدَمَةً أَوْ بَعْضَهَا حُرًّا أَوْ مَرْهُونَةً أَوْ أُمَّ وَلَدٍ فَوَلَدُ كُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ عَلَى مِثَالِ حَالِ أُمِّهِ ، يَعْتِقُونَ بِعِتْقِهَا وَيَرِقُّونَ بِرِقِّهَا /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي مُدَبَّرَةٍ دُبِّرَتْ وَهِيَ حَامِلٌ ، وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ سَيِّدُهَا بِحَمْلِهَا : /10 إِنَّ وَلَدَهَا بِمَنْزِلَتِهَا ، وَإِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ رَجُلٍ أَعْتَقَ جَارِيَةً لَهُ وَهِيَ حَامِلٌ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِحَمْلِهَا /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 فَالسُّنَّةُ فِيهَا ، أَنَّ وَلَدَهَا يَتْبَعُهَا وَيَعْتِقُ بِعِتْقِهَا /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَكَذَلِكَ لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا ابْتَاعَ جَارِيَةً وَهِيَ حَامِلٌ ، فَالْوَلِيدَةُ وَمَا فِي بَطْنِهَا لِمَنِ ابْتَاعَهَا ، اشْتَرَطَ ذَلِكَ الْمُبْتَاعُ أَوْ لَمْ يَشْتَرِطْهُ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَلَا يَحِلُّ لِلْبَائِعِ أَنْ يَسْتَثْنِيَ مَا فِي بَطْنِهَا ، لِأَنَّ ذَلِكَ غَرَرٌ يَضَعُ مِنْ ثَمَنِهَا ، وَلَا يَدْرِي أَيَصِلُ ذَلِكَ إِلَيْهِ أَمْ لَا ؟ وَإِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ مَا لَوْ بَاعَ جَنِينًا فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ ، وَذَلِكَ لَا يَحِلُّ لَهُ ،   لِأَنَّهُ غَرَرٌ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي مُكَاتَبٍ أَوْ مُدَبَّرٍ ابْتَاعَ أَحَدُهُمَا جَارِيَةً ، فَوَطِئَهَا فَحَمَلَتْ مِنْهُ وَوَلَدَتْ ، قَالَ : /10 وَلَدُ كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا مِنْ جَارِيَتِهِ بِمَنْزِلَتِهِ ، يَعْتِقُونَ بِعِتْقِهِ ، وَيَرِقُّونَ بِرِقِّهِ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 فَإِذَا أُعْتِقَ هُوَ ، فَإِنَّمَا أُمُّ وَلَدِهِ مَالٌ مِنْ مَالِهِ يُسَلَّمُ إِلَيْهِ إِذَا أُعْتِقَ /10 .$E424
بَابُ جَامِعِ مَا جَاءَ فِي التَّدْبِيرِ

hadiths.english_translation: Malik said regarding a mudabbar who said to his master: 'Hasten for me the emancipation and I will give you fifty dinars from it in installments upon me.' His master said: 'Yes, you are free, and upon you are fifty dinars - you pay to me each year ten dinars.' The slave agreed to that, then the master perished after that by a day or two or three. Malik said: The emancipation is established for him and the fifty dinars became a debt upon him. His testimony is permitted, his sanctity and inheritance and legal punishments are established, and the death of his master does not waive from him anything of that debt. Malik said regarding a man who granted tadbir to a slave of his, then the master died and he had present wealth and absent wealth, but there was not in his present wealth what would allow the mudabbar to be freed in it: The mudabbar is detained with his wealth, and his earnings are collected until it becomes clear from the absent wealth. If there is in what his master left what the third carries, he is freed with his wealth and with what was collected from his earnings. If there is not in what his master left what carries him, the amount of the third is freed from him and his wealth is left in his hands.

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي مُدَبَّرٍ ، قَالَ لِسَيِّدِهِ : عَجِّلْ لِي الْعِتْقَ وَأُعْطِيكَ خَمْسِينَ مِنْهَا مُنَجَّمَةً عَلَيَّ ، فَقَالَ سَيِّدُهُ : نَعَمْ ، أَنْتَ حُرٌّ ، وَعَلَيْكَ خَمْسُونَ دِينَارًا تُؤَدِّي إِلَيَّ كُلَّ عَامٍ عَشَرَةَ دَنَانِيرَ ، فَرَضِيَ بِذَلِكَ الْعَبْدُ ثُمَّ هَلَكَ السَّيِّدُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ بِيَوْمٍ أَوْ يَوْمَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَاثَةٍ ، قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 يَثْبُتُ لَهُ الْعِتْقُ وَصَارَتِ الْخَمْسُونَ دِينَارًا دَيْنًا عَلَيْهِ ، وَجَازَتْ شَهَادَتُهُ وَثَبَتَتْ حُرْمَتُهُ وَمِيرَاثُهُ وَحُدُودُهُ ، وَلَا يَضَعُ عَنْهُ مَوْتُ سَيِّدِهِ شَيْئًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ الدَّيْنِ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي رَجُلٍ دَبَّرَ عَبْدًا لَهُ ، فَمَاتَ السَّيِّدُ وَلَهُ مَالٌ حَاضِرٌ وَمَالٌ غَائِبٌ ، فَلَمْ يَكُنْ فِي مَالِهِ الْحَاضِرِ مَا يَخْرُجُ فِيهِ الْمُدَبَّرُ ، قَالَ : /10 يُوقَفُ الْمُدَبَّرُ بِمَالِهِ ، وَيُجْمَعُ خَرَاجُهُ حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ مِنَ الْمَالِ الْغَائِبِ ، فَإِنْ كَانَ فِيمَا تَرَكَ سَيِّدُهُ مِمَّا يَحْمِلُهُ الثُّلُثُ ، عَتَقَ بِمَالِهِ وَبِمَا جُمِعَ مِنْ خَرَاجِهِ ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيمَا تَرَكَ سَيِّدُهُ ، مَا يَحْمِلُهُ عَتَقَ مِنْهُ قَدْرُ الثُّلُثِ وَتُرِكَ مَالُهُ فِي يَدَيْهِ /10 .

hadiths.english_translation: Malik said regarding a mudabbar whose master sold him or gave him as a gift or wrote him in mukatabah: His tadbir is nullified by that. Malik said: The explanation of that is that his master had a right in his tadbir as long as he was alive. So if the master freed him from the tadbir, he is permitted to do that. The tadbir is only a bequest that the master bequeathed to him, so if he wishes he changes it. Malik said regarding a mudabbar who committed a crime: His master has no argument with him. Rather, there is taken from the mudabbar's property what fulfills what he injured. If there is not with the mudabbar property that fulfills that, the injured party waits with him until the master dies. If the master leaves what accommodates the value of the mudabbar, he is freed and pays from his own property what he injured. If the master does not leave what accommodates him, the amount that the third carries is freed from him. So if half of him is freed, he pays half of what he injured and the injured party follows him with the remainder if the mudabbar ever has wealth. If the mudabbar does not have wealth, he is enslaved to him in what remains for him, because the portion that was enslaved of the mudabbar is liable for the injuries of all of him.

hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: The practice among us regarding the mudabbar is that he cannot be sold nor given as a gift, nor can his service be bequeathed, nor can he be lent out, nor anything of that which would remove him from the possession of his master. Malik said regarding a mudabbar who has property: If his master dies and the mudabbar is freed by the third, he takes his property. If the third does not carry him and he is freed partially, nothing of his property is taken for what is enslaved of him. That is because when he was granted tadbir, his tadbir was more confirmed than mukatabah. The mukatab works for his mukatabah and is followed for it, but the mudabbar does not work for anything, and nothing is followed from him. He only acquires and holds property. Malik said regarding a mudabbar who dies and his master is alive: His property belongs to his master.

hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 الْأَمْرُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ عَلَيْهِ عِنْدَنَا ، أَنَّ كُلَّ عَتَاقَةٍ أَعْتَقَهَا رَجُلٌ فِي وَصِيَّةٍ أَوْصَى بِهَا فِي صِحَّةٍ أَوْ مَرَضٍ : أَنَّهُ يَرُدُّهَا مَتَى شَاءَ وَيُغَيِّرُهَا مَتَى شَاءَ مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ تَدْبِيرًا ، فَإِذَا دَبَّرَ فَلَا سَبِيلَ لَهُ إِلَى رَدِّ مَا دَبَّرَ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَكُلُّ وَلَدٍ وَلَدَتْهُ أَمَةٌ أَوْصَى بِعِتْقِهَا وَلَمْ تُدَبَّرْ ، فَإِنَّ وَلَدَهَا لَا يَعْتِقُونَ مَعَهَا إِذَا عَتَقَتْ ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ سَيِّدَهَا يُغَيِّرُ وَصِيَّتَهُ إِنْ شَاءَ وَيَرُدُّهَا مَتَى شَاءَ ، وَلَمْ يَثْبُتْ لَهَا عَتَاقَةٌ ، وَإِنَّمَا هِيَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ رَجُلٍ ، قَالَ لِجَارِيَتِهِ : إِنْ بَقِيَتْ عِنْدِي فُلَانَةُ حَتَّى أَمُوتَ ، فَهِيَ حُرَّةٌ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 فَإِنْ أَدْرَكَتْ ذَلِكَ كَانَ لَهَا ذَلِكَ ، وَإِنْ شَاءَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ بَاعَهَا وَوَلَدَهَا ، لِأَنَّهُ لَمْ يُدْخِلْ وَلَدَهَا فِي شَيْءٍ مِمَّا جَعَلَ لَهَا ، قَالَ : وَالْوَصِيَّةُ فِي الْعَتَاقَةِ مُخَالِفَةٌ لِلتَّدْبِيرِ ، فَرَقَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ مَا مَضَى مِنَ السُّنَّةِ ، قَالَ : وَلَوْ كَانَتِ الْوَصِيَّةُ بِمَنْزِلَةِ التَّدْبِيرِ ، كَانَ كُلُّ مُوصٍ لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى تَغْيِيرِ وَصِيَّتِهِ وَمَا ذُكِرَ فِيهَا مِنَ الْعَتَاقَةِ ، وَكَانَ قَدْ حَبَسَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ مَالِهِ مَا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ يَنْتَفِعَ بِهِ /10 .E425 قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي رَجُلٍ دَبَّرَ رَقِيقًا لَهُ جَمِيعًا فِي صِحَّتِهِ ، وَلَيْسَ لَهُ مَالٌ غَيْرُهُمْ : /10 إِنْ كَانَ دَبَّرَ بَعْضَهُمْ قَبْلَ بَعْضٍ ، بُدِئَ بِالْأَوَّلِ فَالْأَوَّلِ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الثُّلُثَ ، وَإِنْ كَانَ دَبَّرَهُمْ جَمِيعًا فِي مَرَضِهِ ، فَقَالَ : فُلَانٌ حُرٌّ وَفُلَانٌ   حُرٌّ وَفُلَانٌ حُرٌّ فِي كَلَامٍ وَاحِدٍ ، إِنْ حَدَثَ بِي فِي مَرَضِي هَذَا حَدَثُ مَوْتٍ أَوْ دَبَّرَهُمْ جَمِيعًا فِي كَلِمَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ، تَحَاصَّوْا فِي الثُّلُثِ وَلَمْ يُبَدَّأْ أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ قَبْلَ صَاحِبِهِ ، وَإِنَّمَا هِيَ وَصِيَّةٌ ، وَإِنَّمَا لَهُمُ الثُّلُثُ ، يُقْسَمُ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْحِصَصِ ، ثُمَّ يَعْتِقُ مِنْهُمُ الثُّلُثُ بَالِغًا مَا بَلَغَ . قَالَ : وَلَا يُبَدَّأُ أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ إِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ كُلُّهُ فِي مَرَضِهِ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي رَجُلٍ دَبَّرَ غُلَامًا لَهُ ، فَهَلَكَ السَّيِّدُ وَلَا مَالَ لَهُ إِلَّا الْعَبْدُ الْمُدَبَّرُ ، وَلِلْعَبْدِ مَالٌ ، قَالَ : /10 يُعْتَقُ ثُلُثُ الْمُدَبَّرِ وَيُوقَفُ مَالُهُ بِيَدَيْهِ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي مُدَبَّرٍ كَاتَبَهُ سَيِّدُهُ فَمَاتَ السَّيِّدُ وَلَمْ يَتْرُكْ مَالًا غَيْرَهُ ، قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 يُعْتَقُ مِنْهُ ثُلُثُهُ وَيُوضَعُ عَنْهُ ثُلُثُ كِتَابَتِهِ ، وَيَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ ثُلُثَاهَا /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي رَجُلٍ أَعْتَقَ نِصْفَ عَبْدٍ لَهُ وَهُوَ مَرِيضٌ ، فَبَتَّ عِتْقَ نِصْفِهِ أَوْ بَتَّ عِتْقَهُ كُلَّهُ وَقَدْ كَانَ دَبَّرَ عَبْدًا لَهُ آخَرَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ ، قَالَ : /10 يُبَدَّأُ بِالْمُدَبَّرِ قَبْلَ الَّذِي أَعْتَقَهُ وَهُوَ مَرِيضٌ ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ لَيْسَ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَرُدَّ مَا دَبَّرَ وَلَا أَنْ يَتَعَقَّبَهُ بِأَمْرٍ يَرُدُّهُ بِهِ ، فَإِذَا عَتَقَ الْمُدَبَّرُ فَلْيَكُنْ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الثُّلُثِ فِي الَّذِي أَعْتَقَ شَطْرَهُ حَتَّى يَسْتَتِمَّ عِتْقُهُ كُلُّهُ فِي ثُلُثِ مَالِ الْمَيِّتِ ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَبْلُغْ ذَلِكَ فَضْلَ الثُّلُثِ عَتَقَ مِنْهُ مَا بَلَغَ فَضْلَ الثُّلُثِ بَعْدَ عِتْقِ الْمُدَبَّرِ الْأَوَّلِ /10 .*E426

hadiths.english_translation: Malik said regarding a mudabbar upon whom is debt to people: The debt is not followed from him in his property if he has property, nor is he sold for it while his master is alive. If his master dies and leaves what carries the mudabbar in his third, the mudabbar is freed and follows the debt from his own property. If he has no property, it is followed from him in his earning and he is not sold. If the master does not leave what carries him, nothing is freed of him and he is not sold either. The creditor waits for the master's heirs to have wealth and then they are made to choose. If they wish, they free the mudabbar from the third of their companion and follow the debt from his earning, and if they wish, they hand him over to the creditor and he uses him in his right which is upon him, not selling him. If the heirs do not have wealth from which the mudabbar can be freed, the creditor waits with what is for him until the mudabbar acquires wealth or the heirs acquire wealth. Then the mudabbar is freed from the third of their companion's wealth and the creditor follows him. Malik said: It is not fitting that the heirs hand over the mudabbar to the creditor permanently and he becomes a slave to him because the tadbir cannot be invalidated, and he was only mudabbar.
